faq.q: Is this page only Fraser Valley land?
faq.a: No — that is the page's title, not its feed. The first cards read for this file include land in Quesnel and Fort St. John (both "Contact for address," no price displayed), Gibsons and Squamish, alongside Langley, Surrey and Mission parcels, and every card read is labelled "Land" and "Status: Active".

faq.q: How many homes can I build on ALR land?
faq.a: Generally one principal residence of 500 m² or less in total floor area (with no more than 1,000 m² of fill for its construction), with a secondary suite permitted only inside that residence; one additional detached residence may also be permitted without an ALC application, capped at 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less or 186 m² on larger parcels, where local bylaws also permit it — more than that, or a larger residence, requires ALC approval.

faq.q: How do I check whether a lot is in the Agricultural Land Reserve?
faq.a: On the Agricultural Land Commission's maps, by PID or civic address; subdivision of reserve land requires ALC permission apart from limited approving-officer cases in the ALR General Regulation.

faq.q: What property transfer tax applies on a land purchase?
faq.a: The general rates are 1% of fair market value up to and including $200,000, 2% of the portion over $200,000 up to and including $2,000,000, and 3% of the portion over $2,000,000, plus a further 2% on the residential portion above $3,000,000, calculated on fair market value at registration unless an exemption applies.
